hints.title: Operand Precedence and Order
hints.text: In postfix notation, operands precede operators. How can you hold incoming numbers until an operation consumes the most recent two?

hints.title: Consuming Most Recent Operands
hints.text: An operator always combines the two most recently accumulated numbers. The second removed value is the left operand and the first removed value is the right operand.

hints.title: Evaluation Procedure with Zero Truncation
hints.text: Iterate through tokens. If token is an integer, record it. If it is an operator, take the two most recent numbers, apply the operation, truncating toward zero for division, and store the result. Return the final remaining number.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of tokens in the expression (1 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Single pass over tokens with O(1) push and pop operations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Repeatedly scanning the string to find operator-operand triplets and splicing them in-place takes O(N^2) time due to array shifts. For N = 10^4, this is too slow.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single linear scan with an auxiliary stack uses O(N) auxiliary space to achieve O(N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Proper handling of integer division truncating toward zero (especially negative numbers in Python: int(a / b) rather than a // b), operand order awareness (left - right, left / right), and single-element edge case.

solutions.approach: Operand Stack with Explicit Zero Truncation
Stack-based Evaluation with Native Integer Division
